This one's a stunner. Today's picture shows a galaxy that's sitting right there in the sky, close enough that you could spot it with a decent pair of binoculars, and yet most people have never heard of it. Why? Because it's hiding behind a thick curtain of dust and stars in our own galaxy. That dust blocks a lot of visible light, so the galaxy looks dim and a little muddy in regular photos. But in infrared, the dust becomes transparent and the spiral arms pop out beautifully. It's a good reminder that what we see depends on the kind of light we look at. If you want to hunt for it yourself, you'll need a dark sky and some patience, but it's worth the effort.
